document.title: Scroll focused controls into view; honour pad buttons held at startup
document.summary: A Scroll now scrolls to show a control the D-pad or autoFocus moves Focus to, the D-pad can reach controls scrolled out of view, and a Pad Button already held when a Deck App starts now reports one onPressStart instead of being ignored.
document.why: D-pad Focus could move to a control inside a Scroll that stayed off screen, and Pad Buttons held at the runtime's first input sample were ignored until pressed again ([#106](source:s1)).

sources.title: Moving focus to a row inside a Scroll does not scroll it into view
sources.gist: Scroll the focused control into view on focus change; treat Pad Buttons held at startup as pressed or document the edge; cover both in input_harness.

sources.label: PR #116
sources.title: fix(input): scroll focused controls into view; honour pad buttons held at startup
sources.gist: Scroll-into-view on focus change and Pad Buttons held at startup press once; fixes #106.

sources.label: Merge-gate review · Oct 26
sources.gist: Blocker: the D-pad cannot reach rows outside a Scroll viewport; low: hover scroll cascades under the pointer; nit: input.h wording.

sources.label: Round-2 review · Oct 26
sources.gist: Unclipping every Scroll let hidden rows compete with controls outside it; unclip only the Scroll that contains Focus, restore viewport-clip expectations, drop the unreachable guard in set_focus_into_view.

parts.name: Focus scroll-into-view
parts.summary: Focus changes from the D-pad and autoFocus scroll every containing Scroll, innermost first, just enough to show the control, and the D-pad can pick controls scrolled out of view inside the Scroll that holds Focus.

parts.name: Held Pad Buttons
parts.summary: A runtime start no longer ignores held Pad Buttons, while the Shell-hide ignore still applies.

groups.title: Scroll a newly focused control into view
groups.why: The issue asks that a focus change into a Scroll adjust its offset so the focused bounds are visible ([#106](source:s1)).
groups.summary: set_focus_into_view in input.c calls the new instance_scroll_into_view for D-pad and autoFocus Focus, which walks the focused instance's parents in the front snapshot and moves each Scroll's offset to the nearest edge that shows its layout bounds, clamped to the content.
lookFor: Mouse hover and mouse press still move Focus but no longer scroll, so a hovered row that is partly hidden stays where it is under the pointer ([review](source:s3)).
A reveal calls touch_stop_momentum, so a D-pad press during a flick stops the glide instead of letting it carry the new Focus off screen.
When the focused control is taller than the viewport, the top edge wins because the top check runs after the bottom one.

groups.title: Let the D-pad reach controls scrolled out of view
groups.why: Without it the D-pad stops at the last row that touches the viewport, so evenly tiled rows below it are unreachable ([review](source:s3)). Unclipping every Scroll let hidden rows steal moves from controls outside it ([round-2 review](source:s4)).
groups.summary: find_nearest_focusable passes the current Focus to get_focusable_elements_for, and collect_focusable_instance clips a Scroll that contains Focus only to its x range, while any other Scroll keeps its viewport clip.
lookFor: Hidden rows inside the focused Scroll share absolute y with whatever sits below it; nearest-centre picks the hidden row first, and test_focus_leaves_scroll checks that Down leaves the Scroll only after its last row.

From outside a Scroll only its visible rows compete: Down from a header enters a bottom-scrolled list at its first visible row, and Up from a Button below enters at the last visible one (test_focus_outside_scroll_header, test_focus_outside_scroll_below).
Perf: subtree_contains_id walks each Scroll subtree on every D-pad move, so a nested Scroll is walked once per enclosing Scroll.
get_focusable_elements (no Focus) keeps viewport clipping, so hit_test_harness expects it to hide scrolled-out rows and get_focusable_elements_for("b1") to keep them.

groups.title: Press Pad Buttons held when a Deck App starts
groups.why: The issue asks to treat buttons held at startup as pressed on the first sample or document the edge ([#106](source:s1)); this takes the first option.
groups.summary: input_clear_focus resets Pad Button states without setting pad_ignore_held, so a held button presses on the next sample unless the Shell hide that preceded the restart already asked to ignore it.
lookFor: A Runtime Upload Replacement restart while the user holds Circle now sends pressstart to the new runtime; a restart from the Shell keeps ignoring it because hide_shell_to_deck sets the ignore before js_runtime_stop and js_runtime_start run.

commits.subject: fix(input): hidden Scroll rows only compete from inside their Scroll
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
get_focusable_elements_for(focused_id) unclips a Scroll's descendants to its width only when the Scroll's subtree contains Focus; otherwise the viewport clips, so hidden rows no longer steal D-pad moves from controls outside the Scroll. find_nearest_focusable passes the current Focus, the no-focus call keeps viewport clipping, and the unreachable guard in set_focus_into_view goes.

Co-Authored-By: Muse Wonder 1.0 <noreply@muse.ai>

commits.subject: fix(input): the D-pad reaches controls scrolled out of view
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Every focusable inside a Scroll is now a navigation candidate, clipped
only to the Scroll's width, so Down from the last visible row reaches
the next hidden one and scrolls it into view. Mouse hover and press no
longer scroll, so the content does not slide under the pointer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(input): press Pad Buttons held when a Deck App starts
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A runtime start no longer ignores Pad Buttons that are already held: the first sample reports onPressStart once, like any new press. A button held when the Shell hides, including the hide that restarts the runtime, is still ignored until released.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(input): scroll a newly focused control into view
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
When Focus moves to a control inside a Scroll (D-pad, autoFocus, mouse hover or press), each Scroll containing it now scrolls by the least that shows its whole layout bounds, innermost first, clamped to the content. Touch momentum stops on a focus change so it cannot carry the control back out; touch drags clear Focus, so they never fight the adjustment.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

summary.before: collect_focusable_instance clips a Scroll's descendants only to the Scroll's x range, so get_focusable_elements returns hidden rows at their scrolled positions and focus_nav_pick can pick them.
summary.after: find_nearest_focusable passes the current Focus to get_focusable_elements_for, and collect_focusable_instance clips a Scroll that contains Focus only to its x range, while any other Scroll keeps its viewport clip.

why.before: Without it the D-pad stops at the last row that touches the viewport, so evenly tiled rows below it are unreachable ([review](source:s3)).
why.after: Without it the D-pad stops at the last row that touches the viewport, so evenly tiled rows below it are unreachable ([review](source:s3)). Unclipping every Scroll let hidden rows steal moves from controls outside it ([round-2 review](source:s4)).

added: Hidden rows inside the focused Scroll share absolute y with whatever sits below it; nearest-centre picks the hidden row first, and test_focus_leaves_scroll checks that Down leaves the Scroll only after its last row.

From outside a Scroll only its visible rows compete: Down from a header enters a bottom-scrolled list at its first visible row, and Up from a Button below enters at the last visible one (test_focus_outside_scroll_header, test_focus_outside_scroll_below).
Perf: subtree_contains_id walks each Scroll subtree on every D-pad move, so a nested Scroll is walked once per enclosing Scroll.
get_focusable_elements (no Focus) keeps viewport clipping, so hit_test_harness expects it to hide scrolled-out rows and get_focusable_elements_for("b1") to keep them.
removed: Hidden rows below a Scroll share absolute y with whatever sits below the Scroll; nearest-centre picks the hidden row first, and test_focus_leaves_scroll checks that Down leaves the Scroll only after its last row.
Children of a nested Scroll stay candidates even when the outer Scroll has scrolled that nested Scroll away; the hit_test_harness expectations flip to match.
